statement: Let m = len(first_string) and n = len(second_string). Let Q be the set of all quadruples (i,j,a,b) such that 0 <= i <= j < m, 0 <= a <= b < n, and the inclusive byte substring first_string[i..j] equals second_string[a..b]. The function returns a result r (it does not fail). If Q is empty, then r = 0. If Q is nonempty, let D = min { j - a | (i,j,a,b) in Q }. Then r = |{ (i,j,a,b) in Q | j - a = D }|.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: For every first_string and second_string satisfying the preconditions, the function returns some result r; it does not fail, overflow, go out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= |C|, where C = { c in {97,98,...,122} | c occurs at least once in first_string and at least once in second_string }. In particular, r <= 26.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: The function returns r and r = 0 if and only if no byte value occurs in both first_string and second_string; equivalently, there are no indices p,q with 0 <= p < len(first_string), 0 <= q < len(second_string), and first_string[p] = second_string[q].
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: The function returns r. If r > 0, then the set Q from S1 is nonempty and there exists a quadruple (i,j,a,b) in Q with j - a = min { y - u | (x,y,u,v) in Q }; that is, at least one minimizing quadruple exists and is included in the count.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r > 0, let Q be the set from spec_1 and D = min { j - a | (i,j,a,b) in Q }. Then -(len(second_string) - 1) <= D <= len(first_string) - 1.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r > 0, let Q and D be as in spec_1. For every (i,j,a,b) in Q with j - a = D, we have i = j and a = b. Equivalently, every optimal matching substring has length 1.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Let C be the set of lowercase bytes c (ASCII 97 through 122) that occur in both strings. If C is empty, then the function returns 0. If C is nonempty, for each c in C let f(c) be the least index p with first_string[p] = c, and let l(c) be the greatest index q with second_string[q] = c. Let D = min_{c in C} (f(c) - l(c)). The function returns r and r = |{ c in C | f(c) - l(c) = D }|.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r > 0, let Q and D be as in spec_1. For every (i,j,a,b) in Q with j > i (equivalently, b > a), we have j - a > D.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r > 0, let Q and D be as in spec_1. For every (i,j,a,b) in Q, let L = j - i + 1 (which equals b - a + 1). Then j - a >= D + L - 1.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r > 0, let D = min { p - q | 0 <= p < len(first_string), 0 <= q < len(second_string), first_string[p] = second_string[q] }. For every pair (p,q) with first_string[p] = second_string[q] and p - q = D, p is the first occurrence of first_string[p] in first_string (there is no p' < p with first_string[p'] = first_string[p]) and q is the last occurrence of second_string[q] in second_string (there is no q' > q with second_string[q'] = second_string[q]).
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Let C be the set of common lowercase bytes. If C is nonempty, for c in C let f(c) and l(c) be as in spec_9 and let D = min_{c in C}(f(c)-l(c)). Then for every c in C, f(c)-l(c) >= D; moreover the number of pairs (p,q) with first_string[p] = second_string[q] = c and p - q = D is 1 if f(c)-l(c) = D and 0 otherwise. The result r equals the sum over c in C of these numbers.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.

statement: Let r be the result on (first_string, second_string). Suppose len(first_string) >= 2 and the last byte of first_string does not occur anywhere in second_string. Let first_string' be first_string with its last byte removed, and let r' be the result on (first_string', second_string). Then the function returns both r and r' and r = r'.
preconditions: first_string and second_string are nonempty slices of bytes, each byte is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97 through 122), and 1 <= len(first_string), len(second_string) <= 200000.
